Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
The options are limited in size, so here's the detail:
Yes, occasionally, I have decks relying on merged vampires Yes, but not frequently (I have decks with a copy of the base or adv version, just in case) No, no merged vampire is worth being in a deck No, I'd like to but it's too slow / too complicated / not worth the effort / doesn't work well (crypt building, merged mecanism)

Please explain why / why not.

Prince of Paris, France

Ratings Coordinator, Rules Director

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
For my part, I find there are some nice vampire once merged, but it's a bit complicated to use them casually.

Star vampires are maybe an exception, because I'd probably include 5 copies of the base version anyway and just add 1 copy of the merged version (or 4+1). It makes the crypt somehow unbalanced but not more than for a star vampire.
Eg. Nergal + Nergal adv

The real trouble is for non-star vampires: it doesn't work well.
Let's take for instance some Carna deck with Valerius Major. You'd probably be forced to play 3 Valerius adv + 1 base, because the advanced version has the nice anti-obf special.
But then your crypt is a bit crippled, and you can't play Epiphany (works only with base version).

If you merge it manually, it takes an extra turn which is quite a penalty when you intend to bring out 2 more vampires.

If you use Wider View, you'll even probably need 1 extra turn to fetch the right version (if you're lucky), for a total of 2 turns.

Messages.Author: extrala
Messages.Body:
Merging vampire generally is interesting, but the mechanics for achieving this are too complicated and too shaky to rely a deck's main strategy on. I have/had a few decks with normal/advanced versions of the same vampire like Goratrix, Sarasine or Theo Bell. But the decks never really relied on merging them.

Maybe it would help to change the rules for merging a bit, e.g. similar to the Anarch Convert effect, you could choose to draw another card from your crypt or alternatively to gain a pool. I was also thinking how it would change things if you further incentivize merging vampires in different ways, for example  Untap the vampire if you're merging them. Gain half the capacity (round down) in blood for the vampire.

Messages.Author: Borrelstein
Messages.Body:
Often the merged vampire is nice to have, but usually only one of the two versions is essential for your deck, so usually I take only one.
However I like some of the new cards such as Sarassine Adv, where you really need to merge if you want to get a powerful special.

Wider View makes it actually quite doable to get merged if you are not in a hurry, and it also has other uses.
Epiphany and Gift of Experience take up card slots and may clog your hand, so you want to include some card cycling tech. For Gift of Experience, tutoring is nice but your vamp gets tapped so you do not have an action.
If you really need a fast merger you can also tutor the missing part with Recruitment, but the 2+1 pool cost makes it worse that Gift of Experience, depending on how much you would value your actions/staying untapped.

Messages.Author: BenPeal
Messages.Body:
> Borrelstein wrote:
> Epiphany and Gift of Experience take up card slots and may clog your hand, so you want to include some card cycling tech.
>
Remember that every non-Advanced crypt card is considered to be a base version, so any non-Advanced vampire can play Epiphany to cycle it, even if they don't have an Advanced version. I have a bunch of decks that involve merging vampires, and my merging package is 8x Epiphany and 2x Wider View. I've found merging to be fairly easy, with negligible hand jam.
